chunks: Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, informed me from Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from Sa'd ibn 'Abd Allah, from Abu Ja'far, from 'Ali ibn Hadid and al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked Aba 'Abd Allah عليه السلام about a man who is returning from his journey, and the time of salat has entered while he is still on the road. He said: He should pray two rak'ahs. And if he sets out on his journey and the time of salat has entered, then he should pray four.

key_terms.أَرْبَعًا: four rak'ahs; the complete prayer of a resident
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rak'ahs; the shortened prayer of the traveler
key_terms.سَفَرِهِ: his journey; the state of travel that affects the ruling of salat
key_terms.فِي الطَّرِيقِ: on the road; not yet arrived at home or destination
key_terms.وَقْتُ الصَّلَاةِ: the time of prayer; the legally designated time when salat becomes due

ai.seo_question: How should a person pray if the time of salat begins while returning from travel or just after departing on a journey?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the ruling of salat when the prayer time enters during a transition between residence and travel. A returning traveler who has not yet reached his people prays in shortened form, while a resident departing on travel after the prayer time has entered prays in complete form.
